items.stem: Which statement best describes what happens during a chemical reaction?

options.text: A substance changes its shape or state but stays the same substance
Bonds are broken and new bonds are formed, creating one or more new substances
Atoms are destroyed and replaced with brand-new atoms
A substance gets hotter or colder without changing in any other way

items.explanation: A chemical reaction transforms substances into NEW substances. Bonds between atoms break and new bonds form - the atoms themselves are never created or destroyed, only rearranged.

items.stem: Why is melting ice NOT a chemical reaction?

options.text: Because it happens too slowly to count as a reaction
Because the ice absorbs heat instead of releasing it
Because no new substance forms - the liquid is still water
Because ice has no chemical bonds to break

items.explanation: The test for a chemical reaction is whether a new substance forms. Melted ice is still water - same molecules, different state. Only the shape and state changed, so it's a physical change.

items.stem: Which observation is the strongest evidence that a chemical reaction has occurred, not just a physical change?

options.text: The material was broken into smaller pieces but is otherwise the same
A gas, a new color, or a new solid appeared that was not there before
The material changed from a liquid to a solid simply by cooling down
The material was poured into a differently shaped container

items.explanation: Signs like bubbling gas, a new color, or a new solid forming are evidence that a brand-new substance was made. Breaking a material, changing its state, or moving it does not make a new substance, so those are physical changes.

items.stem: A hand warmer pouch becomes hot and stays warm for hours after you activate it. What does this tell you about the reaction inside?

options.text: It is exothermic, because it releases thermal energy into the surroundings
It is endothermic, because it pulls heat away from your hand
It is only a physical change, because just the temperature changed
No energy is being transferred into or out of the pouch at all

items.explanation: An exothermic reaction releases thermal energy to its surroundings. The hand warmer feels hot because the reaction inside is sending heat out into your hand and the air around it.

items.stem: An athlete squeezes an instant cold pack and it quickly gets icy cold against her skin. What type of reaction is happening inside, and why?

options.text: Exothermic, because the pack releases coldness into her skin
Exothermic, because the reaction creates heat inside the pack
Endothermic, because the reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, making them colder
Endothermic, because the reaction releases energy as light

items.explanation: An endothermic reaction absorbs energy from the environment. The reaction inside the pack pulls heat IN from its surroundings - including her skin - so the temperature of the environment decreases. Enter = in!

items.stem: You combine two clear liquids. Bubbles of gas form and the beaker turns warm. What is the best conclusion?

options.text: A chemical reaction is likely, because gas forming and a temperature change are signs a new substance formed
It is only a physical change, since both starting materials were liquids
Nothing chemical happened, because the mixture did not change color
Matter was destroyed, because gas escaped from the beaker

items.explanation: Gas production and a temperature change are two classic signs that new substances formed. Color change is not required, and matter is never destroyed - the atoms are simply rearranged into new substances, some of which are gases.

items.stem: Which of these is an example of an exothermic reaction?

options.text: An instant cold pack that chills your skin
Ice slowly melting into liquid water
A puddle of water evaporating on a hot day
Wood burning in a campfire, giving off heat and light

items.explanation: Exothermic reactions release energy to the surroundings. A burning campfire gives off heat and light. The cold pack is endothermic, and melting and evaporating are physical changes, not reactions.

items.stem: During an endothermic reaction, which way does thermal energy move between the reaction and its surroundings?

options.text: Energy moves out of the reaction and into the surroundings, warming them
Energy moves out of the surroundings and into the reaction, cooling them
Energy stays locked inside the reaction and never moves
Cold moves out of the reaction and into the surroundings

items.explanation: Endothermic means energy is absorbed. The reaction pulls thermal energy in from its surroundings, so the surroundings lose heat and cool down. Cold is not a thing that moves; it is just the absence of heat.

items.stem: Two reactions run side by side. Reaction 1 warms the air around it; Reaction 2 cools the air around it. How should they be classified?

options.text: Both are exothermic, since both change the temperature
Reaction 1 is endothermic and Reaction 2 is exothermic
Reaction 1 is exothermic and Reaction 2 is endothermic
Neither can be classified without knowing the exact chemicals

items.explanation: Watch the surroundings. Reaction 1 warms its surroundings, so it releases energy (exothermic). Reaction 2 cools its surroundings, so it absorbs energy (endothermic).

items.stem: A reaction flask feels cold to the touch while the reaction runs. What is happening to the energy?

options.text: The reaction is making cold and pushing it into the flask
The reaction is releasing heat into the room around it
No energy is moving into or out of the reaction at all
The reaction is absorbing heat from its surroundings, so they cool down

items.explanation: Cold is not a thing that gets made or moved - it is the absence of heat. The flask feels cold because the endothermic reaction is pulling heat IN from its surroundings, lowering their temperature.
